newsitem.title: USA: Clinton unveils new application for gun purchase.
newsitem.headline: Clinton unveils new application for gun purchase.

text.p: The U.S. government is issuing a new application to keep guns away from "dangerous drifters" like the foreigner who opened fire on top of the Empire State Building in New York last February, President Bill Clinton said on Thursday.

Speaking at a memorial service for fallen police officers, Clinton said the application was a result of his order to the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms (ATF) to tighten the screening of customers of federally-licensed gun dealers.
"Today, we are releasing a new application to make sure that certification of residency is an unavoidable step for gun purchases. Those who can't prove it can't purchase," he said.

A Danish tourist was killed and six other people wounded when a Palestinian visitor, Ali Abu Kamal, randomly shot at sightseers on the 86th floor observation deck of the Empire State Building on Feb. 23. The man then killed himself.

Kamal bought the .380-calibre semiautomatic 14-shot Beretta used in the New York attack a few weeks after entering the country on Dec. 24, 1996, having moved into a Melbourne, Florida, motel and acquired a state identification card.
Under the new restrictions, aliens have to establish residency in the United States for at least 90 days before they can buy a firearm.

The new applications, being distributed to all 112,000 federally licensed gun dealers, require non-citizens to declare their state of residency and to prove it with documents such as utility bills or lease agreements.
"This is a response to the immediate issue," said Raymond Kelly, Treasury under secretary for enforcement, who oversees the ATF. "This is not going to close every loophole."

Kelly acknowledged during a news conference that the new restrictions alone would not have prevented the Empire State Building shooting, but added, "It would not have happened in the timeframe that it did."

Clinton, the first president in recent times to take on the powerful gun lobby on gun control issues, said the new application was another step "to protect our communities from gun violence by dangerous drifters who threaten our safety."
The president issued an order on March 5 that implemented the tighter restrictions and led to the new application form.

He also called for other gun control measures. They included strengthening the Brady Bill, which prohibits gun purchases by felons, and keeping young criminals from buying guns after they turn 21 and their juvenile records are erased.
